messages:
noah_fin: Hi @rahul_contractor 026-INV-091 came in but AP flagged tax docs. We don't have a W-8 or W-9 on file. Are you invoicing as an individual India resident or a US entity? Need to know which form to collect.

rahul_contractor: Hey Noah 026-INV-091 is from me personally, I'm an India resident sole proprietor (Indian PAN: ABCDE1234F). I saw other vendors sending a W-9 sometimes. Which one should I submit?

samantha_tax: Quick primer: W-9 is for US persons. Non-US persons/entities provide W-8 forms. For individuals in India contracting to a US company, typically we need a W-8BEN (individual) or W-8BEN-E (entity) to certify foreign status and claim treaty benefits.

noah_fin: Thanks. Rahul, can you fill the W-8BEN and attach PAN/ID? Also confirm where the services were performed (India or US).

rahul_contractor: Services fully performed in India (remote dev). I'll attach W-8BEN scanned and my PAN. One Q: my Indian accounting team says India may require TDS (withholding) under Indian law when payment is received from abroad. If Redwood withholds US taxes, can I ask for a gross-up?

withholdbot: :information_source: Automated check: No US backup withholding flagged. But missing W-8BEN means potential default 30% withholding on US-source FDAP income.

kevin_payments: AP note: we can't pay without completed W-8BEN. If services are performed entirely outside US and are non-US source, US withholding shouldn't apply, but docs still required to avoid withholding.

samantha_tax: Correct. Key points: 1) Source of income for services is generally where services are performed. If done in India, not US-source -> no US withholding. 2) W-8BEN will certify foreign status and can claim treaty if relevant (India-US treaty re: dependent personal services is limited). 3) Indian TDS is a separate issue; Redwood paying from US typically isn't responsible for Indian TDS unless contract says so.

rahul_contractor: Hmm contract says "gross-up for withholding only if required by law." My firm says they sometimes withhold 10% TDS for payments to foreign individuals under Indian rules when money hits a local bank. Will Redwood consider a gross-up to cover Indian TDS?

noah_fin: We don't normally gross-up for vendor-side local tax unless pre-approved in SOW/contract. We need procurement/legal sign-off + pricing approval.

samantha_tax: Also: if Indian TDS is applied, vendor can often claim foreign tax credit in India. Gross-up would increase our costs; it's not our standard. Recommend vendor provide proof of actual TDS if they want discussion for reimbursement.

kevin_payments: Operational: Rahul please upload the signed W-8BEN (PDF) and PAN. We'll hold payment until docs received. If any withholding occurs we will escalate to legal/finance for decision on gross-up.

rahul_contractor: Uploaded W-8BEN (link: https://files.example/rahul/w8ben-2026.pdf) and PAN scan. If we later need to request gross-up I'll open a ticket with evidence of Indian TDS.

withholdbot: :no_entry: Payment blocked: W-8 form required/received but under review.

noah_fin: Thanks Rahul. Marking as on-hold. @samantha_tax and @legal please advise if we should include a clause in future SOWs clarifying that Redwood won't gross-up for foreign personal taxes.

samantha_tax: Agree we should add standard language: "Vendor responsible for local taxes; Redwood will not gross-up unless explicitly agreed in writing." I'll draft a clause and share.

kevin_payments: Once W-8BEN validated and we confirm service location, AP can release. If vendor later demonstrates Indian TDS was deducted and requests gross-up, they must provide official certificate (Form 16A equivalent).

rahul_contractor: Appreciate the clarity. Will wait for payment release once validation done. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
